![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14167856/assets/ddb73fe5746933a3a08acc3fe2a370fbe91a944b22f5b94be1425907f83c0fed.png)

Determine the equation of the line shown above if its slope is $\frac{1}{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ We know that the slope is $m=\frac{1}{2},$ so we just need to work out $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line passes through the point $(2,4).$ Substituting this into $y=mx+b$ with $m=\frac{1}{2}$ and solving for $b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}x+b \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{2}(2)+b \\ 4 & =1+b \\ b & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is $y=\frac{1}{2}x+3.$
